beats.text: In July 1931, the governor of Oklahoma declared martial law over a bridge south of Durant. Then he showed up wearing a pistol.
beats.label: SOUTH OF DURANT, OKLAHOMA

beats.text: A new free bridge over the Red River, linking Durant and Denison, Texas, was finished. But the owners of the old toll bridge got a federal court order to keep it closed.
beats.label: JULY 1931
beats.credit: Texas Historical Commission marker; Texas State Library and Archives

beats.text: Texas barricaded its end, and Texas Rangers were sent to guard it.
beats.label: THE TEXAS SIDE
beats.credit: Oklahoma Today; Texas Historical Commission marker

beats.text: Oklahoma's governor, Alfalfa Bill Murray, had the barricades torn down, and later called out the National Guard.
beats.label: ALFALFA BILL MURRAY

beats.text: They called it the Red River Bridge War. No one was hurt.
beats.label: NO ONE WAS HURT

beats.text: The free bridge officially opened on Labor Day, 1931, and carried traffic until the 1990s.
beats.label: LABOR DAY, 1931
beats.credit: Oklahoma Today; Texas Historical Commission marker

beats.text: A piece of it still sits in the city park in Colbert, Oklahoma.
beats.label: COLBERT, OKLAHOMA
beats.credit: Oklahoma Today; Oklahoma marker at the span

beats.text: Comment your town, and it could be next.
